new.permit_q193_q: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
new.permit_q193_a0: Speed up so that you clear the intersection before the red
new.permit_q193_a1: The light is about to turn red, so begin to slow down
new.permit_q193_a2: Stop at once, even if you are already in the intersection
new.permit_q193_a3: Go on with care, the same as at a flashing yellow light
new.permit_q193_exp: A steady yellow light means caution: the light is about to change to red. Begin to slow down. The yellow light gives cars already in the intersection time to leave it.
new.permit_q194_q: You face a red light with a green arrow. What may you do?
new.permit_q194_a0: Stay stopped until the round light turns green, because a red light overrules a green arrow shown with it
new.permit_q194_a1: Go in the direction of the arrow; other traffic must yield to you
new.permit_q194_a2: Go carefully in the direction of the arrow, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians
new.permit_q194_a3: Go straight or turn either way, as long as the way is clear
new.permit_q194_exp: A red light with a green arrow means you may go carefully in the direction of the arrow. You must still yield to other vehicles and to pedestrians.
new.permit_q195_q: What does a steady red arrow mean?
new.permit_q195_a0: Stop: you may not make that turn until the arrow turns green
new.permit_q195_a1: The turn lane ahead is closed, so move over and turn from another lane
new.permit_q195_a2: Turn with care after yielding to oncoming cars
new.permit_q195_a3: You may turn that way after a full stop, the same as at a stop sign
new.permit_q195_exp: A steady red arrow means stop if you want to turn the way the arrow points. Wait until the arrow turns green.
new.permit_q196_q: A steady red "X" is lit above your lane. What does it mean?
new.permit_q196_a1: This lane is for left turns
new.permit_q196_a3: Do not drive in this lane
new.permit_q196_exp: Some highways use overhead lane lights. A steady red X means do not drive in this lane. A green arrow means you may use the lane.
new.permit_q197_q: There is more than one traffic light at an intersection. Which one do you obey?
new.permit_q197_a0: The one that is closest to you
new.permit_q197_a1: The one directly over your lane
new.permit_q197_a2: The one on the far right side
new.permit_q197_a3: The one that turns green first
new.permit_q197_exp: When there is more than one traffic light, obey the one that is directly over your lane.
new.permit_q198_q: What shape and color are most warning signs?
new.permit_q198_a0: Rectangular, white with black letters or symbols
new.permit_q198_a1: Round, yellow with a black X and two letters
new.permit_q198_a3: Triangular, red and white, with the point down
new.permit_q198_exp: Warning signs tell you about danger ahead. They are usually diamond-shaped and yellow, with black letters or symbols. Slow down when you see one.
new.permit_q199_q: What do regulatory signs (white with black, red, or green letters) tell you?
new.permit_q199_a0: Dangers ahead, such as curves, merges, and crossings
new.permit_q199_a1: Where to find services such as fuel, food, lodging, hospitals, and rest areas
new.permit_q199_a2: Directions to towns, exits, and points of interest
new.permit_q199_a3: Rules you must follow, such as speed, turns, lane use, and parking
new.permit_q199_exp: Regulatory signs give rules: traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking. They are white with black, red, or green letters or symbols.
new.permit_q200_q: A sign shows a red circle with a red slash across a symbol. What does it mean?
new.permit_q200_a0: Use extra care when you do what the symbol shows
new.permit_q200_a1: You may not do what the symbol shows
new.permit_q200_a2: What the symbol shows is allowed at this place
new.permit_q200_exp: A red circle with a red slash means NO. You may not do what the symbol shows, such as turn left or make a U-turn.
new.permit_q201_q: What do black-and-white speed limit signs show?
new.permit_q201_a0: The legal speed when conditions are ideal
new.permit_q201_a1: The speed you should hold, whatever the weather
new.permit_q201_a2: A suggested speed that police do not enforce
new.permit_q201_a3: The lowest speed you may drive on that road
new.permit_q201_exp: A speed limit sign shows the legal speed when conditions are ideal. In rain, snow, fog, or heavy traffic you must drive slower.
new.permit_q202_q: You come to a stop sign. There is no stop line and no crosswalk. Where must you stop?
new.permit_q202_a0: Level with the stop sign itself, even if you cannot see the cross street from there
new.permit_q202_a1: A car length into the intersection, so that you can see past parked cars and hedges on both sides
new.permit_q202_a2: At the point nearest the intersection where you can see traffic, before any part of your car enters it
new.permit_q202_a3: Anywhere within about 30 feet of the intersection, as long as you are fully stopped
new.permit_q202_exp: Stop behind the stop line or crosswalk if there is one. If there is none, stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can see traffic on the other road. No part of your car may be in the intersection.
new.permit_q203_q: What does a "Shared Center Lane — Left Turn Only" sign mark?
new.permit_q203_a0: A passing lane that drivers from both directions take turns using
new.permit_q203_a1: A lane for left turns only, used by traffic from either direction
new.permit_q203_a2: A lane for through traffic when the other lanes are full
new.permit_q203_a3: A lane where left turns are banned during rush hour
new.permit_q203_exp: A shared center lane is only for vehicles turning left. Traffic from either direction may use it. It is not for through traffic or for passing.
new.permit_q204_q: What does a ONE WAY sign tell you?
new.permit_q204_a0: The lane beside you ends in the direction of the arrow
new.permit_q204_a1: Trucks must follow the arrow; cars may go either way
new.permit_q204_a2: Parking is allowed on the side the arrow points to
new.permit_q204_a3: Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow
new.permit_q204_exp: On a one-way street, traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow. Do not turn against the arrow, and do not drive the wrong way.
new.permit_q205_q: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the light is red. What do you do?
new.permit_q205_a0: Obey the light, not the officer
new.permit_q205_a1: Follow the car ahead of you
new.permit_q205_exp: If police are directing traffic, do as they direct. Police have the authority to direct all traffic. When police are not there, signs and signals have the force of law.
new.permit_q206_q: Guide signs are square or rectangular. What colors are they?
new.permit_q206_exp: Guide signs are green, brown, or blue. They point the way to roads, towns, and points of interest, and help you find hospitals, fuel, food, and hotels.
new.permit_q207_q: A two-way road has a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line down the middle. When may you pass?
new.permit_q207_a0: When the dashed line is on your side and the way is clear
new.permit_q207_a1: When the solid line is on your side, and the way is clear
new.permit_q207_a2: From either side of the road, as long as the way ahead is clear
new.permit_q207_a3: At no time: two yellow lines mean no passing for both sides
new.permit_q207_exp: Sometimes one yellow line is solid and the other is dashed. Then only traffic with the dashed line on its side may pass, and only when it is safe.
new.permit_q208_q: What do two solid yellow lines down the middle of a road mean?
new.permit_q208_a0: Passing is allowed for both directions when the way is clear
new.permit_q208_a2: No passing for traffic in either direction
new.permit_q208_a3: No left turns into driveways or side streets
new.permit_q208_exp: Two solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited in both directions.
new.permit_q209_q: What do broken white lines between lanes tell you?
new.permit_q209_a0: Traffic in the next lane is coming toward you
new.permit_q209_a1: You must stay in your lane until the line ends
new.permit_q209_a2: The lane beside you is for buses and bicycles
new.permit_q209_a3: The lanes go the same way, and you may change lanes when safe
new.permit_q209_exp: Broken white lines mark lanes going in the same direction. You may change lanes when it is safe.
new.permit_q210_q: What does a solid white line between two lanes going the same way mean?
new.permit_q210_a0: Traffic on the other side of the line is coming toward you
new.permit_q210_a1: The lanes have different uses, and changing lanes is discouraged
new.permit_q210_a2: You may pass on either side of the line at highway speeds
new.permit_q210_a3: The lane on the other side of the line is closed to all traffic for now
new.permit_q210_exp: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same way that have different uses, such as a turn lane. They discourage changing lanes.
new.permit_q211_q: A vehicle ahead has an orange triangle with a red border on its back. What does it tell you?
new.permit_q211_a0: It is a slow-moving vehicle, going 25 mph or less
new.permit_q211_a1: It is carrying a wide load that may hang into your lane
new.permit_q211_a2: It is a driver education car with a student at the wheel
new.permit_q211_a3: It has broken down and is waiting for a tow truck to come
new.permit_q211_exp: The orange triangle with a red border is the slow-moving vehicle sign. Farm tractors, animal-drawn carts, and road maintenance vehicles use it. They usually go 25 mph or less. Slow down early and pass only when it is safe.
new.permit_q212_q: What does a white, X-shaped sign that says "RAILROAD CROSSING" tell you to do?
new.permit_q212_a0: Come to a full stop each time, even with no train
new.permit_q212_a1: Speed up, so you spend less time on the tracks
new.permit_q212_a2: Stop behind the stop line or before the tracks if a train is coming
new.permit_q212_a3: Stop on the tracks and look both ways before going on
new.permit_q212_exp: The white X-shaped sign marks the crossing itself. If a train is coming, you must stop behind the stop line or before the tracks. Look both ways and never stop on the tracks.
new.permit_q213_q: Which two signs mark a place where you may not pass?
new.permit_q213_a0: A yellow diamond on the right and a green rectangle on the left
new.permit_q213_a1: A yellow pennant on the left and a white DO NOT PASS sign on the right
new.permit_q213_a2: An orange diamond on either side of the road
new.permit_q213_a3: A red octagon on the right and a white X-shaped sign on the left side of the road
new.permit_q213_exp: A yellow pennant sign on the left of the road says NO PASSING ZONE. A white rectangular sign on the right says DO NOT PASS. You may not pass where you see either sign.
new.permit_q214_q: A flagger in a work zone signals you to stop, but the lane ahead looks clear. What must you do?
new.permit_q214_a0: Go slowly if the lane is clear
new.permit_q214_a1: Stop, then go if no one is coming
new.permit_q214_a2: Follow the car ahead of you
new.permit_q214_exp: A flagger may direct traffic in a work zone. You must do as the flagger directs, even when the road looks clear to you.
new.permit_q215_q: May you turn right at a red light in Maine?
new.permit_q215_a0: Yes, after a full stop, unless a sign says no; yield to people and traffic
new.permit_q215_a1: Yes, without stopping, if no traffic is coming from the left
new.permit_q215_a2: No. A right turn at a red light is against Maine law
new.permit_q215_a3: Yes, but in daylight hours and not after dark or in rain
new.permit_q215_exp: A right turn at a red light is allowed after you stop, unless a sign says otherwise. You must yield to pedestrians and to all other traffic first.
new.permit_q216_a0: A phone call or text, but not eating or talking
new.permit_q216_a1: Anything that takes your mind or body away from driving
new.permit_q216_a2: Something outside the car, such as a crash scene
new.permit_q216_a3: A problem that affects new drivers, not skilled ones
new.permit_q216_exp: A distraction is anything that takes your mind or body away from driving. Phones, food, passengers, and your own thoughts can all be distractions.
new.permit_q217_q: What are the three types of driver distraction?
new.permit_q217_a1: Inside the car, outside the car, and weather
new.permit_q217_exp: Visual distractions take your eyes off the road. Manual distractions take your hands off the wheel. Cognitive distractions take your mind off driving. Most crashes involve two or all three.
new.permit_q218_q: You look at a billboard as you drive past. What type of distraction is that?
new.permit_q218_a0: Visual: your eyes leave the road
new.permit_q218_a1: Manual: your hands leave the wheel
new.permit_q218_a2: Cognitive: your mind leaves the task
new.permit_q218_a3: None, because you are still steering
new.permit_q218_exp: A visual distraction makes you look away from the road. You look at something that has nothing to do with driving, such as a billboard or a crash scene.
new.permit_q219_q: Which of these is a manual distraction?
new.permit_q219_a0: Worrying about a test you have at school today
new.permit_q219_a1: Looking at a crash on the other side of the road
new.permit_q219_a2: Listening to a friend tell a long, funny story
new.permit_q219_a3: Reaching for a drink or tuning the radio
new.permit_q219_exp: A manual distraction takes one or both hands off the wheel. Your hands do something that is not driving. Examples are eating, drinking, tuning the radio and setting a GPS.
new.permit_q220_q: You are angry and upset as you drive. What type of distraction is that?
new.permit_q220_a0: Visual: you cannot see as well when upset
new.permit_q220_a1: Cognitive: your mind is not on driving
new.permit_q220_a2: Manual: you grip the wheel too hard
new.permit_q220_a3: It is not a distraction if your eyes stay on the road
new.permit_q220_exp: Cognitive distractions are thoughts and feelings that pull your mind away from the road. Anger, anxiety and worry are examples.
new.permit_q221_q: What should you do with your phone and GPS before you start to drive?
new.permit_q221_a0: Hold the phone in your hand so you can answer quickly
new.permit_q221_a1: Set the GPS at the first red light, while the car is stopped
new.permit_q221_a2: Turn off the phone and set the GPS before you leave
new.permit_q221_a3: Put the phone on the dash where you can read texts at a glance
new.permit_q221_exp: Prevent distractions before you drive: turn off your phone, set the navigation, finish eating, and secure loose items. When driving, do not talk on the phone and do not text.
new.permit_q222_q: You are stopped at a red light in Maine. May you read or send a text?
new.permit_q222_a0: No. The texting ban still applies when you are stopped in traffic
new.permit_q222_a1: Yes. The law covers moving vehicles, so a stopped car at a light does not count
new.permit_q222_a2: Yes, if you are 18 or older and use one hand
new.permit_q222_a3: Yes, if you finish before the light turns green
new.permit_q222_exp: Maine bans texting while you operate a vehicle on a public way. That includes when you are stopped for traffic, a traffic light, or a stop sign. Pull safely off the road first.
new.permit_q223_q: You are 16 with an intermediate license and need to make a call. What does Maine law require?
new.permit_q223_a0: Use the speaker so that your hands stay on the wheel
new.permit_q223_a1: Keep the call under one minute and use one hand
new.permit_q223_a2: Wait for a stop sign or a red light, then make the call
new.permit_q223_a3: Pull off the road and stop in a safe place before you use the phone
new.permit_q223_exp: A licensed driver under 18 may not use a phone while driving, even when stopped at a light or in traffic. You may use it once you have pulled over to the side of, or off, the road and stopped where the car can safely stay.
new.permit_q224_q: In a study the Maine driver's manual cites, which distraction was by far the most dangerous one seen?
new.permit_q224_exp: The manual cites a study of truck drivers in which texting was by far the most dangerous distraction. Texting takes your eyes, your hands, and your mind off driving at the same time.
new.permit_q225_q: How does the Maine driver's manual say to travel with a pet?
new.permit_q225_a0: On your lap, where you can keep the animal calm
new.permit_q225_a1: Loose on the back seat, with a window open a little for air
new.permit_q225_a2: In a pet carrier, not loose in the vehicle
new.permit_q225_a3: In the front seat, held in a passenger's arms
new.permit_q225_exp: Keep pets in a pet carrier, not loose in the vehicle. A loose animal can climb on you, block the pedals, or pull your eyes off the road.
new.permit_q226_q: Your friends in the back seat start to argue loudly while you drive. What is the best thing to do?
new.permit_q226_a0: Turn around for a moment to tell them to stop, then look back at the road
new.permit_q226_a1: Do not join in; keep your mind on driving, and pull over if you need to
new.permit_q226_a2: Join in, but keep one hand on the wheel and glance back
new.permit_q226_a3: Watch them in the rearview mirror until they calm down, and drive from memory
new.permit_q226_exp: Do not argue with passengers while you drive. Get rid of things that take your mind away from driving: it is your job to drive safely. If you cannot ignore it, pull over in a safe place.
new.permit_q227_q: How does the Maine driver's manual compare crashes caused by phone distraction with crashes caused by impaired driving?
new.permit_q227_a0: They are less serious, because the driver is sober
new.permit_q227_a1: They happen at low speeds, so few people are hurt
new.permit_q227_a2: They are rare, because most drivers can multitask
new.permit_q227_a3: They can be just as serious and as deadly
new.permit_q227_exp: The manual says that using a phone or other device in a moving vehicle can cause crashes. Those crashes can be as serious as the ones that impaired drivers cause.
new.permit_q228_q: The Maine manual says to stop at least how far from a person in the roadway who has a white cane or a guide dog?
new.permit_q228_exp: A person with a white cane or a guide dog has the right of way. Stop at least 10 feet away and wait until the person is out of danger.
new.permit_q229_q: A cyclist is riding on your right, and you want to turn right. What does Maine law say?
new.permit_q229_a0: Turn only when you can do it safely and without interfering with the cyclist
new.permit_q229_a1: Speed up and turn in front of the cyclist before they reach the corner
new.permit_q229_a2: Turn at once; the cyclist must brake, because cars have the right of way
new.permit_q229_a3: Tap the horn and turn, since a signal gives you the right to go first
new.permit_q229_exp: A driver near a cyclist may not turn right unless the turn can be made safely and without getting in the way of the cyclist. Slow down and let the cyclist clear the corner first.
new.permit_q230_q: You are turning left. A cyclist is coming toward you from the other direction. Who must yield?
new.permit_q230_a0: The cyclist must yield to you
new.permit_q230_a1: The one who is moving slower
new.permit_q230_a2: You must yield to the cyclist
new.permit_q230_exp: A driver turning left must yield to a cyclist coming from the opposite direction, the same as for an oncoming car. Turn only when it is safe.
new.permit_q231_q: When should you use your horn near a cyclist?
new.permit_q231_a0: Each time you pass, so they know you are there
new.permit_q231_a1: When they are riding too far out in the lane
new.permit_q231_a2: At night, because bikes are hard to see
new.permit_q231_a3: Only when there is a chance of a crash
new.permit_q231_exp: Do not use your horn close to a cyclist unless there is a chance of a crash. The horn can startle the rider and make them steer into your path.
new.permit_q232_q: Under Maine law, how is a bicycle on the road treated?
new.permit_q232_a0: As a pedestrian, so it should use the sidewalk
new.permit_q232_a1: As a vehicle, with the same rights and duties as other drivers
new.permit_q232_a2: As a slow vehicle that must pull over each time a car comes up behind it
new.permit_q232_a3: As a non-vehicle, with no right to the travel lane
new.permit_q232_exp: Bicycles are considered vehicles. A cyclist has the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers and has a legal right to use the road.
new.permit_q233_q: On a road too narrow for a car and a bike side by side, where may the cyclist ride?
new.permit_q233_a0: On the far edge, or else off the road
new.permit_q233_a2: In or near the center of the lane
new.permit_q233_a3: On the sidewalk, since the road is closed to bikes there
new.permit_q233_exp: When a road is too narrow for cars and bikes to travel side by side, a cyclist should "take the travel lane" by riding in or near the center. Stay behind until you can pass with at least 3 feet of space.
new.permit_q234_q: When may you drive or park in a bicycle lane?
new.permit_q234_a0: Only when entering or leaving an alley or driveway
new.permit_q234_a1: When you need to get around a car that is waiting to turn left
new.permit_q234_a2: When you can see that no cyclists are using the lane
new.permit_q234_a3: For up to five minutes, to drop off or pick up a passenger
new.permit_q234_exp: Do not stop, park, or drive in a bicycle lane unless you are entering or leaving an alley or driveway. Yield to cyclists where a bike lane or path crosses the road.
new.permit_q235_q: You are driving out of a driveway across a sidewalk. What must you do?
new.permit_q235_a0: Pull across the sidewalk first, then stop at the curb so that you can see the cars coming
new.permit_q235_a1: Stop before the sidewalk and wait for pedestrians and traffic
new.permit_q235_a2: Roll slowly across while sounding your horn
new.permit_q235_a3: Yield to cars, but people on the sidewalk must wait for you
new.permit_q235_exp: Cars coming out of a driveway or alley must stop before the sidewalk and wait for pedestrians and traffic. You must yield to everyone on the sidewalk.
new.permit_q236_q: Your light is green, but a person is still crossing in front of you. What do you do?
new.permit_q236_a0: Go, because a green light gives you the right of way
new.permit_q236_a1: Tap the horn and move forward slowly
new.permit_q236_a2: Drive around the person on the side with more room
new.permit_q236_a3: Yield and let the person finish crossing
new.permit_q236_exp: Yield to all pedestrians even if the traffic light is green. A green light means go only when the way is clear of traffic and people.
new.permit_q237_q: About how far ahead do your headlights let you see clearly at night?
new.permit_q237_exp: Headlights let you see clearly only about 250 feet ahead. Do not drive faster than you can stop in that distance.
new.permit_q238_a0: Leaving your high beams on when another car is coming toward you at night
new.permit_q238_a1: Using your headlights in the daytime, which wears the bulbs out
new.permit_q238_a2: Driving so fast that you cannot stop within the distance your lights show
new.permit_q238_a3: Driving at night with one headlight burned out
new.permit_q238_exp: Never drive so fast that you cannot stop within the distance you can see ahead with your lights. If your stopping distance is longer than your headlight range, you will see a hazard too late to stop.
new.permit_q239_q: On a dark road, above about what speed does the Maine manual say you are "driving blind" with your headlights?
new.permit_q239_exp: Headlights show about 250 feet. The manual's chart gives a total stopping distance of 188 feet at 50 mph and 272 feet at 60 mph. So above about 50 mph you cannot stop inside the distance you can see.
new.permit_q240_q: You are using high beams at night. When must you switch to low beams?
new.permit_q240_a0: Within 500 feet of an oncoming car, or 300 feet behind a car
new.permit_q240_a1: Within 100 feet of an oncoming car, or 50 feet behind a car
new.permit_q240_a2: When the other driver flashes their lights at you
new.permit_q240_a3: At the town line, where street lights begin
new.permit_q240_exp: Dim your headlights when you come within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or follow within 300 feet of a vehicle. If an oncoming driver does not dim, slow down and look toward the right side of the road.
new.permit_q241_q: You get your first Maine license at age 19. For how long is it a provisional license?
new.permit_q241_exp: The first license issued to a new driver under 21 is provisional for two years. (The law says two years or until you turn 21, whichever is later.) For a new driver who is 21 or older, it is provisional for one year.
new.permit_q242_q: You have a provisional license and are convicted of a moving violation. What happens the first time?
new.permit_q242_a0: You get a written warning for the first offense
new.permit_q242_a1: Your license is suspended for 30 days
new.permit_q242_a2: You pay a fine, but you keep your license
new.permit_q242_a3: You must take the road test again within 30 days
new.permit_q242_exp: If you are convicted of a moving violation while your license is provisional, you get a 30-day suspension the first time. The second and third times, the suspension is longer.
new.permit_q243_q: For a provisional license holder, how long is the suspension for a SECOND moving violation?
new.permit_q243_exp: A moving violation suspends a provisional license. The first time it is for 30 days. The second time it is for 180 days. The third time or later it is for one year.
new.permit_q244_q: You get your first Maine license at age 20. Does it stop being provisional when you turn 21?
new.permit_q244_a0: No. It lasts the full two years from the day the license was issued
new.permit_q244_a1: Yes. Provisional rules stop on the 21st birthday
new.permit_q244_a2: Yes, if the driver has had no violations so far
new.permit_q244_a3: No. It lasts until the driver passes a second road test
new.permit_q244_exp: If your first license was issued before your 21st birthday, it is provisional for a full two years. The provisional period does not end when you turn 21.
new.permit_q245_q: In the Maine point system, at how many demerit points does the Secretary of State send a warning?
new.permit_q245_exp: Maine gives demerit points for convictions of certain traffic offenses. A warning is sent at 6 points. At 12 points or more, the license is suspended.
new.permit_q246_q: In the Maine point system, what happens when a driver reaches 12 demerit points?
new.permit_q246_a0: The driver must retake the written test
new.permit_q246_a1: The points are erased and the count starts over
new.permit_q246_a3: The driver gets a warning letter
new.permit_q246_exp: When the point total reaches 12 or more, the driver's license is suspended. The warning comes earlier, at 6 points.
new.permit_q247_q: How long do demerit points stay on a Maine driving record?
new.permit_q247_a1: For three years from the conviction
new.permit_q247_a2: For as long as you hold a license
new.permit_q247_a3: Until they are one year old
new.permit_q247_exp: Points are erased from a driver's record when they become one year old.
new.permit_q248_q: You are in a crash and someone is hurt. What does Maine law say you must do?
new.permit_q248_a0: Stop, stay at the scene, give your name and address, and help the injured
new.permit_q248_a1: Stop and give your insurance card, then you are free to drive away
new.permit_q248_a2: Drive straight to the nearest police station or hospital and report the crash from there
new.permit_q248_a3: Wait in your car without speaking until your insurer calls you
new.permit_q248_exp: You must stop at once, stay at the scene, and give your name and address and your vehicle's registration number. Show your license and proof of insurance if asked. Give reasonable help to anyone who is hurt, and call 911.
new.permit_q249_q: A crash must be reported to the police if anyone is hurt, or if the property damage is at least how much?
new.permit_q249_exp: If a crash involves any injury, or property damage of $2,000 or more, the drivers must report it to the police. Failing to report can bring criminal charges and a license suspension.
new.permit_q250_q: How close may you follow a fire truck that is answering an alarm?
new.permit_q250_a3: As close as you like, with your hazard lights on
new.permit_q250_exp: It is against the law to follow within 500 feet of a fire truck that is responding to a fire alarm.
new.permit_q251_q: What does Maine law require about insurance for a vehicle you drive?
new.permit_q251_a0: Insurance is a good idea, but the law does not require it
new.permit_q251_a1: The owner must be insured, but you need no proof when you borrow a car from a friend or relative
new.permit_q251_a2: You need insurance once you have caused your first crash
new.permit_q251_a3: It must have liability insurance, and you must show proof if an officer asks
new.permit_q251_exp: Maine law says every owner and every driver of a motor vehicle must have liability insurance. You must show proof of it when a police officer asks. Keep the insurance card in the vehicle.
new.permit_q252_q: You borrow a friend's car. Does it need to be insured for you to drive it?
new.permit_q252_a0: No. Insurance is the owner's concern, not the driver's
new.permit_q252_a1: Yes. Any vehicle you drive must be insured, even if you do not own it
new.permit_q252_a2: No, if you are driving it for less than a day
new.permit_q252_a3: Yes, on highways, but not on town streets near home
new.permit_q252_exp: Any vehicle you are operating must be insured even though you are not the owner. Check that the car is insured and that proof of insurance is in it before you drive.
new.permit_q253_q: A police car behind you turns on its blue lights to stop you. What should you do first?
new.permit_q253_a0: Stop right away in your own lane, wherever you happen to be
new.permit_q253_a1: Drive on at the speed limit until you reach a parking lot you know, however far that is
new.permit_q253_a2: Move to the right side of the road and stop in a safe spot
new.permit_q253_a3: Slow down and wave the officer past you on the left-hand side
new.permit_q253_exp: If you are pulled over by the police, move to the right side of the road and make sure you are in a safe spot. Then turn off the engine and turn on your hazard flashers.
new.permit_q254_q: You have been pulled over by the police. What does the Maine manual tell you to do while you wait?
new.permit_q254_a0: Get out, close the door, and walk back to the police car to meet the officer halfway
new.permit_q254_a1: Take off your seat belt and look for your papers in the glove box
new.permit_q254_a2: Call a parent on your phone before you speak to the officer
new.permit_q254_a3: Stay in the car, keep your seat belt on, and keep your hands on the wheel
new.permit_q254_exp: Stay in the vehicle unless you are asked to get out. Stay calm, keep your seat belt fastened, and keep your hands on the steering wheel. Roll down your window so you and the officer can talk.
new.permit_q255_q: It is night and the police have pulled you over. What extra step does the manual give?
new.permit_q255_a0: Turn off your headlights and dash lights to save the battery
new.permit_q255_a1: Turn on your inside lights so the officer can see in
new.permit_q255_a2: Keep your high beams on so the officer can see the road
new.permit_q255_a3: Shine your phone light toward the officer's car
new.permit_q255_exp: At night, turn on your inside lights so the officer can see inside the vehicle. Keep your hands on the wheel where they can be seen.
new.permit_q256_q: The officer asks for your license and registration. They are in the glove box. What should you do?
new.permit_q256_a0: Tell the officer where they are, then reach for them slowly
new.permit_q256_a1: Reach for them quickly so the stop takes less time
new.permit_q256_a2: Say you will bring them to the police station later
new.permit_q256_a3: Ask a passenger to search the car for them
new.permit_q256_exp: The officer may ask for your license, insurance card, or registration. Tell the officer where they are, and reach for them slowly with one hand on the wheel. Then answer the officer's questions.
new.permit_q257_q: Must you show your license to a police officer who asks to see it?
new.permit_q257_a0: No, unless the officer has a written warrant
new.permit_q257_a1: Yes, but only after a crash
new.permit_q257_a2: Yes. You must show it to any officer who asks
new.permit_q257_a3: No. You may mail a copy within 10 days
new.permit_q257_exp: Carry your license with you whenever you drive. You must show it to any police officer who asks to see it. It is illegal to lend your license to anyone else.
new.permit_q258_q: You turn left from a two-way street onto a street with two lanes going your way. Which lane do you turn into?
new.permit_q258_a0: The rightmost lane, to stay out of the way
new.permit_q258_a1: The leftmost lane going in your direction
new.permit_q258_a2: Either lane, as long as you signal before you turn
new.permit_q258_a3: The lane that has the fewest cars in it at the time
new.permit_q258_exp: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from. On a left turn, that is the leftmost lane going in your direction. Change lanes only after the turn is finished.
new.permit_q259_q: You are stopped, waiting to turn left. Why should you keep your front wheels straight?
new.permit_q259_a0: Straight wheels let the engine idle with less strain
new.permit_q259_a1: Turned wheels wear out the tires while you wait
new.permit_q259_a2: Turned wheels make the power steering pump overheat if the wait is longer than a minute
new.permit_q259_a3: If you are hit from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic
new.permit_q259_exp: Do not turn the wheels before you make the turn. If you are struck from behind with the wheels turned, you may be pushed forward into oncoming traffic.
new.permit_q260_q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
new.permit_q260_a0: When it is turning left and there is room, or on a road with two or more lanes going your way
new.permit_q260_a1: When the driver ahead is going under the speed limit and will not move over
new.permit_q260_a2: When you can use the paved shoulder to get around the car
new.permit_q260_a3: Whenever you signal first and sound your horn to warn them
new.permit_q260_exp: Pass on the left in general. You may pass on the right only when the other car is making a left turn and there is room, or when the road has two or more marked lanes going your way. Never drive off the pavement to pass.
